title: What share of trusted validators must agree before an XRPL ledger is validated?
abstract: Sourced guide to the XRP Ledger validation quorum, what happens when validators go offline, and how it differs from the thresholds inside a consensus round.
body:
According to the XRPL Negative UNL documentation, the standard quorum requirement for validating a ledger is 80% of trusted validators. If more than 20% of trusted validators go offline or become unable to communicate with the rest of the network, servers stop validating new ledgers because they cannot reach a quorum. [1]

The Negative UNL lets the network count only the validators that are online. To prevent the network from fragmenting, the quorum has a hard minimum of 60% of total validators. [1]

According to the XRPL consensus protections documentation, a large majority of trusted validators would have to collude to confirm an invalid transaction, at least 80% of them, and if more than about 20% of validators are unreachable or not behaving properly, the network fails to reach a consensus. Inside a consensus round the inclusion threshold is lower and rises: participants first include a transaction if 50% or more of other participants agree, then raise this to 60% and higher. [2][3]

Author interpretation: for an agent, a payment is settled when it appears in a validated ledger, which is the point at which the quorum has agreed; a provisional result from a single server is not final. The 80% quorum for validation and the rising thresholds inside a round are different numbers. These are integration recommendations, not measured guarantees. Sources accessed 11 November 2026. [1][2][3]
